memory_lessons.applicability: When combining N-body optimizations, measure each complete program; improvements to reuse or arithmetic do not necessarily compose.
memory_lessons.claim: The T1+T2 integration was correct but measured 0.001566 s, slower than the correct T1 base at 0.000888 s. The T3 arithmetic proposal has no measured source program because its generation failed, so it remains unverified.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Check the T1-based arithmetic variant against all correctness cases, then compare fresh timings with T1 and the prior integration.

proposal.hypothesis: On the fastest correct tiled base, computing acceleration directly removes the per-interaction target-mass multiplication and final per-target mass division. Using rsqrtf(distSq) cubed also avoids sqrt and division in each interaction. The reassociation and approximate reciprocal square root may affect numerical results, so this is only a hypothesis until the controller checks correctness and measures it.

retained: Retain T1's 128-thread, one-target-per-thread mapping and 256-source shared-memory tiles.
Accumulate acceleration directly by cancelling the positive target mass from the force and final division.
Replace sqrt/division-based inverse-distance cubing with rsqrtf(distSq) and two multiplications.
